paragraphs: Amgen Inc. (including its subsidiaries, referred to as "Amgen," "the Company," "we," "our" or "us") discovers, develops, manufactures and delivers innovative medicines to fight some of the world's toughest diseases. We focus on areas of high unmet medical need and leverage our expertise to strive for solutions that dramatically improve people's lives, while also reducing the social and economic burden of disease. We helped launch the biotechnology industry more than 45 years ago and have grown to be one of the world's leading independent biotechnology companies. Our robust pipeline includes potential first-in-class medicines at all stages of development. We have a presence in approximately 100 countries worldwide.
Amgen was incorporated in California in 1980 and became a Delaware corporation in 1987. Amgen operates in one operating segment: human therapeutics.

Following is a summary of significant developments affecting our business that have occurred and that we have reported since the filing of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024.

In August 2025, we announced that the FDA broadened the approved use of Repatha to include adults at increased risk for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) due to uncontrolled low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), removing the previous requirement that a patient have been diagnosed with cardiovascular (CV) disease.

In November 2025, we announced detailed results from the Phase 3 VESALIUS-CV clinical trial, which showed that Repatha achieved statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in MACEs in high-risk adults without a prior heart attack or stroke, when added to statins or other LDL-C–lowering treatments. Repatha demonstrated a 25% relative reduction in the risk of a composite of coronary heart disease (CHD) death, heart attack or ischemic stroke (3-P MACE), and a 19% reduction in a broader composite that also included any ischemia-driven arterial revascularization (4-P MACE). Repatha also reduced the risk of heart attack by 36%. In a cohort of patients included in a lipid sub-study, the median achieved LDL-C was 45 mg/dL compared to 109 mg/dL in the placebo arm. No new safety signals were identified, and tolerability was consistent with the current prescribing information in the United States.

In April 2025, we announced the FDA approved UPLIZNA for the treatment of Immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) in adult patients. UPLIZNA is the first and only FDA approved treatment for adults living with IgG4-RD.

In December 2025, we announced the FDA approved UPLIZNA for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adults who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) and anti-muscle specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) antibody positive.

In June 2025, we announced interim results from the global Phase 3 DeLLphi-304 trial evaluating IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA in patients with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) who had progressed on or after one line of platinum-based chemotherapy. The study demonstrated that IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA significantly reduced the risk of death by 40% compared to standard-of-care chemotherapy, with a median overall survival of 13.6 months compared to 8.3 months. Additionally, IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA showed a statistically significant improvement in median progression-free survival of 4.2 months compared to 3.7 months and enhanced patient-reported outcomes related to cancer-associated symptoms, including dyspnea and cough. The safety profile of IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA was consistent with prior studies.

In November 2025, we announced that the FDA granted full approval for IMDELLTRA for the treatment of adult patients with extensive stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy, converting its prior accelerated approval to full approval based on results from the global Phase 3 DeLLphi-304 study.

In October 2025, we announced that the FDA approved TEZSPIRE as an add-on maintenance treatment of inadequately controlled chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older.
In June 2025, the European Commission granted marketing authorization approval of TEPEZZA for treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease (TED).

In March 2025, we announced the initiation of two global Phase 3 studies to evaluate MariTide, a differentiated antibody-peptide conjugate that activates the glucagon like peptide 1 (GLP-1) receptor and antagonizes the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR), in chronic weight management: one study in adults living with obesity or overweight without Type 2 diabetes and another study in adults living with obesity or overweight with Type 2 diabetes.

In June 2025, the underlying details from Part 1 of the Phase 2 study of MariTide and complete results from the primary analysis of the Phase 1 pharmacokinetics low dose initiation (PK-LDI) study evaluating lower starting doses of MariTide were presented at the American Diabetes Association 85th Scientific Sessions and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

In November 2025, we announced that, in addition to the two global Phase 3 studies announced in March 2025, four global Phase 3 studies were underway, with studies in adults living with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight; in adults living with heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction and obesity; in adults living with obstructive sleep apnea on positive airway pressure therapy and living with obesity or overweight; and in adults living with obstructive sleep apnea not on positive airway pressure therapy and living with obesity or overweight.

paragraphs: Regulation by government authorities in the United States and other countries is a significant factor in the production and marketing of our products and our ongoing R&D activities. To clinically test, manufacture and market products for therapeutic use, we must satisfy mandatory procedures and safety and effectiveness standards established by various regulatory bodies. Compliance with these standards is complex, and failure to comply with any of these standards can result in significant implications. See Item 1A. Risk Factors for a discussion of factors, including global regulatory implications, that can adversely impact our development and marketing of commercial products.

In the United States, the Public Health Service Act; the FDCA; and the regulations promulgated thereunder as well as other federal and state statutes and regulations govern, among other things, the production, research, development, testing, manufacture, quality control, labeling, storage, record keeping, approval, advertising, promotion and distribution of our products in addition to the reporting of certain payments and other transfers of value to healthcare professionals and teaching hospitals.

Clinical Development and Product Approval. Drug development in our industry is complex, challenging and risky, and failure rates are high. Product development cycles are typically very long—approximately 10 to 15 years from discovery to market. A potential new medicine must undergo many years of preclinical and clinical testing to establish its safety and efficacy for use in humans at appropriate dosing levels and with an acceptable risk–benefit profile. We continue to work toward reducing cycle times by applying our expertise in human genetics and innovation in technology, clinical trials and real-world evidence. See Research and Development and Selected Product Candidates section below.
After laboratory analysis and preclinical testing in animals, we file an IND with the FDA to begin human testing. Typically, we undertake an FDA-designated three-phase human clinical testing program.
•In Phase 1, we conduct small clinical trials to investigate the safety and proper dose ranges of our product candidates in a small number of human subjects.

•In Phase 2, we conduct clinical trials to investigate side-effect profiles and the efficacy of our product candidates in a patient population larger than Phase 1 but still relatively small, who have the disease or condition under study.

MD&A is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Our results of operations discussed in MD&A are presented in conformity with GAAP. Amgen operates in one operating segment: human therapeutics. Therefore, our results of operations are discussed on a consolidated basis.

Amgen Inc. (including its subsidiaries, referred to as "Amgen," "the Company," "we," "our" or "us") discovers, develops, manufactures and delivers innovative medicines to fight some of the world's toughest diseases. We focus on areas of high unmet medical need and leverage our expertise to strive for solutions that dramatically improve people's lives, while also reducing the social and economic burden of disease. We helped launch the biotechnology industry more than 45 years ago and have grown to be one of the world's leading independent biotechnology companies. Our robust pipeline includes potential first-in-class medicines at all stages of development.

Our principal products are Prolia, Repatha, Otezla, ENBREL, EVENITY, XGEVA, TEPEZZA, BLINCYTO, Nplate, TEZSPIRE, KYPROLIS, Aranesp, KRYSTEXXA and Vectibix. We also market a number of other products, including but not limited to MVASI, PAVBLU, UPLIZNA, IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA, AMJEVITA/AMGEVITA, TAVNEOS, Neulasta, LUMAKRAS/LUMYKRAS, RAVICTI, Parsabiv, Aimovig, WEZLANA/WEZENLA and PROCYSBI. For additional information about our products, see Part I, Item 1. Business—Marketing, Distribution and Selected Marketed Products.

Our strategy is the integrated set of actions we take to improve our competitive position in the industry. In 2025, we generated strong sales growth across our product portfolio and regions; advanced our innovative pipeline; and continued to expand and enhance our world-class manufacturing network. We accomplished these objectives while maintaining a strategic and disciplined approach to capital allocation, including retiring $6.0 billion of debt.

In 2025, we achieved several significant regulatory, clinical and operational milestones. We obtained multiple regulatory approvals, including new indications for UPLIZNA and TEZSPIRE; a broadened FDA approval for Repatha; and full FDA approval for IMDELLTRA for the treatment of ES-SCLC. We also advanced our innovative pipeline, including the initiation of six global Phase 3 clinical studies for MariTide and the reporting of Phase 3 data across several programs. In addition, we continued to invest in expanding and enhancing our manufacturing capacity, including facilities in Ohio, North Carolina and the U.S. territory of Puerto Rico. Furthermore, in 2025 we also broke ground on a new state-of-the-art R&D facility in Thousand Oaks, California, to further enhance collaboration and innovation across R&D and process development activities. For additional information on our pipeline and clinical development updates, see Part I, Item 1. Business—Research and Development and Selected Product Candidates, and Part I, Item 1. Business—Significant Developments. For additional information on our manufacturing operations, see Part I, Item 1. Business—Manufacturing, Distribution and Raw Materials.
Total product sales increased 10% in 2025, driven by volume growth of 13%, partially offset by declines in net selling price of 3%.

Cash flows from operating activities in 2025 totaled $10.0 billion, which supported investment in our business, including capital expenditures of $1.9 billion to enhance and expand our manufacturing network, and allowed us to both reduce our debt and return capital to shareholders through the payment of cash dividends. For 2025, we retired $6.0 billion of debt and increased our quarterly cash dividend by 6% to $2.38 per share of common stock. In December 2025, the Board of Directors declared a cash dividend of $2.52 per share of common stock for the first quarter of 2026, an increase of 6% over the same period in the prior year, to be paid in March 2026.

Amgen's approach to human capital management focuses on attracting, developing and retaining a highly skilled global workforce to support the discovery, development and commercialization of innovative medicines. Our compensation, benefits and development programs are designed to promote performance, accountability, adherence to Company values and alignment with shareholder interests. We believe our culture supports innovation, collaboration and productivity as we execute on our mission to serve patients. For additional information, see Part I, Item 1. Business—Human Capital Resources.

We have a long-standing ambition to be environmentally responsible, and we regularly set targets to challenge ourselves to deliver further improvements. As part of our environmental sustainability efforts, we have established long-term targets to meet by 2027, including achieving carbon neutrality, reducing water consumption by 40% and reducing waste disposed by 75%.2,3

Our long-term success depends, to a great extent, on our ability to continue to discover, develop and commercialize innovative products and acquire or collaborate on therapies currently in development by other companies. We must grow sales from existing and new products to achieve revenue growth and to offset revenue losses caused by products' loss of their exclusivity or launches of competing products. For example, our patents for RANKL antibodies, including sequences, for Prolia and XGEVA expired in February 2025 in the United States and in November 2025 in select countries in Europe. Certain of our products face increasing pressure from competition, including biosimilars and generics. For additional information, including information on the expirations of patents for various products, see Part I, Item 1. Business—Marketing, Distribution and Selected Marketed Products—Patents, and Part I, Item 1. Business—Marketing, Distribution and Selected Marketed Products—Competition. We devote considerable resources to R&D activities, but successful product development in the biotechnology industry is highly uncertain. We also face increasing regulatory scrutiny of safety and efficacy both before and after products launch.

Recent and ongoing changes in U.S. trade and tariff policies, including the imposition, modification, suspension and threatened expansion of tariffs on imported goods, as well as retaliatory measures by foreign governments, have increased uncertainty in the overall business and operating environment. Numerous tariffs and trade protection measures have been proposed, and in a number of cases, implemented by the United States and other countries, including the April 2025 Tariff EO, which imposed a universal 10% tariff on goods imported into the United States, with certain exceptions including pharmaceuticals. Further, there were previous proposals for sector-specific tariffs on our industry, and in December 2025, in recognition of our capital investments in U.S. manufacturing, we received relief from Section 232 tariffs, pending final determination under such section of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, for approximately the next three years. Tariffs and trade protection measures may adversely affect our business and results of operations. For additional discussion of these and other risks, see Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors, of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Uncertain macroeconomic conditions, including the risk of inflation, fluctuating interest rates and instability in the financial system, as well as rising healthcare costs, continue to pose challenges to our business. Uncertainty around tariffs and trade protection measures in the United States and other countries, including the imposition, modification, suspension and threatened expansion of tariffs on imported goods, along with ongoing geopolitical conflicts and rising geopolitical tensions, continue to create additional uncertainty in global macroeconomic conditions. Additionally, with public and private healthcare-provider focus, the industry continues to be subject to cost containment measures and significant pricing pressures, resulting in net price declines.

Moreover, provisions of the IRA, as well as the expanded utilization of the 340B Program, have negatively affected, and are likely to continue to negatively affect, our business. For example, CMS has selected ENBREL and Otezla for Medicare price setting beginning in 2026 and 2027, respectively. In addition to the IRA, other recent and proposed U.S. policy actions focus on drug pricing, including the Most-Favored-Nations Prescription Drug Pricing Executive Order (MFN EO) and the July MFN Letter that was delivered to a number of pharmaceutical companies, including Amgen. paragraphs: Amgen Inc. (包括其子公司，簡稱為 "Amgen," "the Company," "we," "our" 或 "us") 發現、開發、製造並交付創新藥物，以對抗一些世界上最困難的疾病。我們專注於高未滿足醫療需求的領域，並運用我們的專業知識，努力尋求能大幅改善人們生活的解決方案，同時也降低疾病的社會與經濟負擔。我們在45年前協助啟動了生物技術產業，並成長為全球領先的獨立生物技術公司之一。我們強大的產品研發管道包括在各階段開發中的潛在首創新藥。我們在全球約100個國家擁有業務據點。
Amgen 於1980年在加州成立，並於1987年成為德拉瓦州公司。Amgen 運作於一個運營分部：人用療效藥物。
以下為影響我們業務的重大發展，這些發展已發生且我們已報導，自我們提交2024年12月31日財年年度報告（Form 10-K）後。
2025年8月，我們宣佈美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）擴大批准Repatha的使用範圍，包括因未控制低密度脂蛋白膽固醇（LDL-C）而增加重大心血管事件（MACE）風險的成人，移除了先前要求患者必須診斷出心血管（CV）疾病的條件。

2025年11月，我們宣佈來自Phase 3 VESALIUS-CV臨牀試驗的詳細結果，顯示Repatha在未經心臟病發作或中風病史的高風險成人中，當與他汀類藥物或其他LDL-C降低治療搭配使用時，可達到統計上顯著且臨牀上有意義的MACE減少。Repatha顯示出對冠狀動脈疾病（CHD）死亡、心臟病發作或缺血性中風（3-P MACE）的組合風險降低25%，並對更廣泛的組合（4-P MACE）降低19%，該組合也包含任何缺血驅動的動脈再血管化。Repatha也降低心臟病發作風險36%。在血脂子研究中包含的患者羣組中，達到的中位數LDL-C為45 mg/dL，與安慰劑組的109 mg/dL相比。未發現新的安全性訊號，且耐受性與美國現行處方資訊一致。
2025年4月，我們宣佈美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准UPLIZNA用於治療免疫球蛋白G4相關疾病（IgG4-RD）的成人患者。UPLIZNA是美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准用於治療IgG4-RD成人患者的首個且唯一藥物。
2025年12月，我們宣佈美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准UPLIZNA用於治療廣泛性肌無力症（gMG）的成人患者，這些患者為抗乙醯膽鹼受體（AChR）和抗肌肉特異性酪胺酸 kinase（MuSK）抗體陽性。

2025年6月，我們宣佈來自全球Phase 3 DeLLphi-304試驗的中期結果，評估IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA在小細胞肺癌（SCLC）患者中，這些患者在使用過一線含鉑化療後的表現。該研究顯示IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA顯著降低40%的死亡風險，與標準療法化療相比，中位總體存活期為13.6個月，與8.3個月相比。此外，IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA在中位無進步存活期方面顯示出統計上顯著的改善，為4.2個月，與3.7個月相比，並改善與癌症相關症狀的患者報告結果，包括氣短和咳嗽。IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA的安全性資料與先前研究一致。
2025年11月，本公司宣佈美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）已授予IMDELLTRA完整批准，用於治療曾接受含鉑化療後疾病持續惡化的成人廣泛期小細胞肺癌（ES-SCLC）患者，將其先前的加速批准轉為完整批准，基於全球第三期DeLLphi-304研究的結果。
2025年10月，本公司宣佈美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）已批准TEZSPIRE作為對 inadequately controlled 慢性鼻竇炎伴鼻息肉（CRSwNP）成人及12歲以上兒童患者的附加維持治療。
2025年6月，歐盟委員會已授予TEPEZZA市場許可批准，用於治療中度至重度甲狀腺眼病（TED）成人患者。
2025年3月，本公司宣佈啟動兩項全球第三期研究，評估MariTide，一種差異化的抗體-肽結合物，可活化胰高血糖素類肽1（GLP-1）受體並拮抗葡萄糖依賴性胰島素釋放肽受體（GIPR），用於慢性體重管理：一項研究針對有肥胖或過重但無第二型糖尿病的成人，另一項研究針對有肥胖或過重且有第二型糖尿病的成人。
2025年6月，MariTide第二期研究第一部分的基礎資料，以及MariTide藥動學低劑量起始（PK-LDI）研究的主要分析結果，已於美國糖尿病協會（ADA）第85屆科學會議中發表，並同時刊登於《新英格蘭醫學期刊》（The New England Journal of Medicine）。
2025年11月，本公司宣佈，除了2025年3月宣佈的兩項全球第三期研究外，另有四項全球第三期研究正在進行中，分別針對有確診動脈粥狀硬化性心血管疾病及肥胖或過重的成人；有心衰竭伴輕度射血分數降低或射血分數輕度降低且肥胖或過重的成人；有阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症並接受正壓通氣治療且有肥胖或過重的成人；以及有阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症但未接受正壓通氣治療且有肥胖或過重的成人。

paragraphs: 以下之管理討論與分析（MD&A）旨在協助讀者瞭解Amgen之業務。MD&A為財務報表及其附註之補充說明，應與之併讀。MD&A中所討論之營運成果係依美國會計準則（GAAP）編製。Amgen從事單一營運分部：人用治療藥物。因此，我們之營運成果係以合併基礎討論。

本報告及其他我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交之文件包含前瞻性聲明，這些聲明係基於目前預期、估計、預測及展望，關於我們、我們未來表現、我們業務、我們信念及我們管理階層之假設。此外，我們或由我們代表之人，可能在正常營運過程中，透過會議、網路直播、電話會議及研討會等，於新聞稿、書面聲明或與投資人及分析師之溝通與討論中，做出前瞻性聲明。如「預期」、「預期」、「展望」、「可能」、「目標」、「預測」、「意圖」、「計畫」、「相信」、「追求」、「估計」、「應」、「可能」、「假設」及「持續」等詞彙，以及這些詞彙之變體及相似表達，係用以識別此類前瞻性聲明。這些聲明並非未來表現之保證，且涉及某些風險、不確定性及假設，這些難以預測。我們於第一部分，第1A項「風險因素」中說明我們所面臨之風險、不確定性及假設，這些可能影響結果或營運成果。我們所做出之前瞻性聲明係基於我們管理階層之信念及假設，這些假設係基於我們管理階層在聲明做出時所掌握之資訊。我們提醒您，實際結果與我們前瞻性聲明所表達、暗示或預測之內容可能有重大差異。特別提及與產品銷售、監管活動、臨牀試驗結果、給付、費用、每股盈餘（EPS）、流動性及資本資源、趨勢、預計股息、股票回購及合作相關之前瞻性聲明。除非美國證券法規及SEC之規則與規範另有規定，否則我們無意或義務在本報告發佈後更新任何前瞻性聲明，無論是否因新資訊、未來事件、假設變更或其他因素所致。

Amgen Inc.（包括其子公司，簡稱為「Amgen」、「本公司」、「我們」、「我們的」或「我們」）發現、開發、製造並交付創新藥物，以對抗世界一些最困難的疾病。我們專注於高未滿足醫療需求之領域，並運用我們的專業知識，追求能大幅改善人們生活之解決方案，同時也降低疾病的社會與經濟負擔。我們在45年前協助啟動了生物技術產業，並已成長為全球領先的獨立生物技術公司之一。我們強大之產品管道包含在各開發階段之潛在首創新藥物。

我們之主要產品為Prolia、Repatha、Otezla、ENBREL、EVENITY、XGEVA、TEPEZZA、BLINCYTO、Nplate、TEZSPIRE、KYPROLIS、Aranesp、KRYSTEXXA及Vectibix。我們亦行銷若干其他產品，包括但不限於MVASI、PAVBLU、UPLIZNA、IMDELLTRA/IMDYLLTRA、AMJEVITA/AMGEVITA、TAVNEOS、Neulasta、LUMAKRAS/LUMYKRAS、RAVICTI、Parsabiv、Aimovig、WEZLANA/WEZENLA及PROCYSBI。有關我們產品之更多資訊，請參閱第一部分，第1項「業務—行銷、分銷及選定行銷產品」。
我們之策略為我們為提升在產業中競爭地位所採取之整合性行動。2025年，我們在產品組合及地區實現強勁銷售成長；推進創新產品管道；並持續擴展與增強我們的世界級製造網路。我們在維持戰略且嚴謹之資本配置方式下達成這些目標，包括償還60億美元之債務。

2025年，我們達成若干重大之監管、臨牀及運營里程碑。我們獲得多項監管核准，包括UPLIZNA及TEZSPIRE之新適應症；Repatha之廣泛FDA核准；以及IMDELLTRA用於治療ES-SCLC之完整FDA核准。我們亦推進創新產品管道，包括MariTide之六項全球第三期臨牀試驗啟動，以及多個計畫之第三期臨牀試驗數據報告。此外，我們持續投資於擴展與增強製造能力，包括Ohio、North Carolina及美國屬地波多黎各之設施。此外，2025年我們亦在千橡市（Thousand Oaks, California）啟動一項新穎尖端之研發設施，以進一步增強研發與製程開發活動之間之合作與創新。有關我們產品管道及臨牀發展更新之更多資訊，請參閱第一部分，第1項「業務—研究與開發及選定產品候選藥物」，以及第一部分，第1項「業務—重大發展」。有關我們製造運營之更多資訊，請參閱第一部分，第1項「業務—製造、分銷及原材料」。
2025年總產品銷售額成長10%，主要因銷售量成長13%，部分抵銷淨銷售價格下降3%之影響。
2025年營運活動之現金流入為100億美元，用以支應對業務之投資，包括19億美元之資本支出以增強與擴展製造網路，並使我們得以同時減少債務並回饋資本給股東，透過現金股息支付。2025年，我們償還60億美元之債務，並將季度現金股息提高6%至每股普通股2.38美元。2025年12月，董事會宣佈於2026年第一季支付每股普通股2.52美元之現金股息，較前一年同期提高6%，預計於2026年3月支付。
Amgen 的人力資本管理方式著重於吸引、培養及留住高素質的全球員工，以支持創新藥物的發現、開發與商業化。我們的薪酬、福利及發展方案設計用以促進績效、責任感、遵守本公司價值觀及與股東利益一致。我們相信本公司文化支持創新、合作與生產力，以執行我們服務病患的使命。有關更多資訊，請參閱第一部分，項目 1. 企業—人力資源。
我們有長期的願景要成為環境責任的企業，並定期設定目標來挑戰自己以實現進一步改善。作為環境永續的行動之一，我們已設立長期目標，預計於 2027 年達成，包括實現碳中和、減少 40% 的用水量及減少 75% 的廢棄物處理量。

我們的長期成功在很大程度上取決於我們持續發現、開發與商業化創新產品，以及取得或與其他公司合作開發目前尚在研發中的療法。我們必須透過現有及新產品的銷售成長來實現營收成長，並抵銷因產品失去專利保護或競爭產品上市所造成的營收減損。例如，我們針對 RANKL 抗體的專利，包括序列，用於 Prolia 和 XGEVA 的專利於 2025 年 2 月在美國到期，並於 2025 年 11 月在部分歐洲國家到期。某些產品面臨來自競爭的壓力，包括生物相似藥與一般藥品。有關更多資訊，包括各產品專利到期資訊，請參閱第一部分，項目 1. 企業—行銷、分銷與主要產品—專利，以及第一部分，項目 1. 企業—行銷、分銷與主要產品—競爭。我們投入大量資源於研發活動，但生物技術產業的產品開發成功具有高度不確定性。我們也面臨對產品安全與有效性日益嚴格的監管審查，無論是在產品上市前或上市後。

美國貿易與關稅政策的近期與持續變動，包括對進口商品課徵、修改、暫停及威脅擴張關稅，以及外國政府的報復措施，已增加整體營運環境的不確定性。已提出許多關稅與貿易保護措施，並在多數情況下已實施，包括 2025 年 4 月的關稅行政命令，對進口至美國的商品課徵普遍 10% 的關稅，但藥品除外。此外，曾有針對我們產業的產業特定關稅提案，並在 2025 年 12 月，因我們在美國製造的資本投資，我們獲得來自 1962 年貿易擴張法案第 232 節的關稅減免，預計持續約三年。關稅與貿易保護措施可能對我們的業務與營運結果產生負面影響。有關這些及其他風險的進一步討論，請參閱第一部分，項目 1A. 風險因素，本年度 10-K 表報表。
不確定的總體經濟環境，包括通貨膨脹風險、利率波動及金融體系不穩定，以及醫療保健成本上升，持續對我們的業務造成挑戰。美國及其他國家的關稅與貿易保護措施的不確定性，包括對進口商品課徵、修改、暫停及威脅擴張關稅，加上持續的國際政治衝突與升溫的國際政治緊張，持續造成全球總體經濟環境的額外不確定性。此外，公共與私人醫療提供者關注，產業持續受到成本控制措施與顯著的定價壓力，導致淨價格下降。

此外，IRA 的條款以及 340B 計畫的擴大使用，已對我們的業務產生負面影響，並可能持續產生負面影響。例如，CMS 已選定 ENBREL 和 Otezla 作為 Medicare 定價的對象，分別自 2026 年及 2027 年開始。除了 IRA，其他近期及提案的美國政策行動聚焦於藥價，包括最優惠國待遇藥價行政命令（MFN EO）以及於 2025 年 7 月發送給多家藥廠，包括 Amgen 的 MFN 信函。在 2025 年 12 月，我們宣佈

headings: 研究與開發及選定產品候選品項
第2期臨牀試驗探討產品候選品項在較大規模病患族羣中的副作用與療效，但樣本數仍相對較少，且這些病患患有正在研究的疾病或狀況。
第1期臨牀試驗探討產品候選品項的安全性與適當劑量範圍，通常在少量人體受試者中進行。
分子 地區 一般主題 預估過期日（1）
paragraphs: 美國及其他國家政府機關的規範為我們產品之生產與行銷以及持續進行之研發活動的重要因素。為臨牀測試、製造與行銷用於治療用途之產品，我們必須符合各相關監管機構所訂定之強製程序及安全與有效性標準。遵守這些標準相當複雜，未能遵守任何一項標準可能產生重大後果。請參閱第 1A 項風險因素，以瞭解可能對我們商業產品之開發與行銷產生負面影響之因素，包括全球監管影響。
在美國，公共衛生服務法；食品、藥物與化妝品法；以及其下所頒布之規則，以及其他聯邦與州法律與規則，規範我們產品之生產、研究、開發、測試、製造、品質控制、標籤、儲存、記錄保存、核准、廣告、推廣與分銷，以及向醫療專業人員與教學醫院報告某些付款及其他價值轉移事項。

臨牀開發與產品核准。我們產業之藥物開發過程複雜、具有挑戰性且風險高，失敗率也相當高。產品開發週期通常非常長，從發現到上市約需 10 到 15 年。潛在的新藥必須經歷多年之預臨牀與臨牀測試，以確立其在人類使用時的安全性與有效性，並在適當劑量水平下，且具有可接受之風險與效益評估。我們持續努力縮短開發週期，透過應用我們在人類遺傳學之專業知識與資訊科技、臨牀試驗與實證醫學之創新技術。請參閱下述之研究與開發及選定產品候選藥物部分。
在完成實驗室分析與動物預臨牀測試後，我們向 FDA 提交 IND 以開始人類測試。通常，我們會進行 FDA 指定之三階段人類臨牀測試計畫。
•在第一階段，我們進行小型臨牀試驗，以探討我們產品候選藥物在少量人類受試者中之安全性與適當劑量範圍。
•在第二階段，我們進行臨牀試驗，以探討我們產品候選藥物之副作用特徵與其在較為廣泛但仍然相對較小之患者羣體（患有所研究之疾病或狀況）中之有效性。
